subject: IaC review: private deployment templates and CI/CD for AcmeFin
messages:
From: Rachel Gomez <rachel.gomez@acmefin.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment IaC review: AcmeFin VPC + on-prem connector

Hi Dev / team,

Thanks again for taking this on. We're just starting our internal review for a private deployment that will sit inside AcmeFin's Azure VNet (primary) and a small on-prem test cluster behind a perimeter firewall. High level asks:

- We need a vetted Terraform module set for VPC/subnet creation that enforces private endpoints and restrictive NSGs.
- Helm charts for the Redwood runtime that allow using customer KMS or existing HSM (we have a Thales cluster).
- Ansible playbooks for initial host bootstrap (ntp, mtusize, docker/containerd config) and security hardening.
- CI/CD flow: GitHub Actions -> Argo CD or similar. We need to show an audited pipeline with linting, static scans, and artifact signing.

I'll attach the network diagram and an initial requirements doc in Drive (link below). Can we run a quick sync this week to review the modules and identify gaps?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Gomez
Head of Platforms, AcmeFin

Attachment stubs: network-diagram-acmefin.pdf (diagram), acmefin-iac-requirements.md
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Gomez <rachel.gomez@acmefin.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment IaC review: AcmeFin VPC + on-prem connector

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear list. I've kicked off an internal review and attached our current artifacts for the AcmeFin pilot so you can see the starting point. Short summary of what I included:

- terraform/modules/vpc: opinionated VPC module enforcing no public subnets by default, explicit route table attachments, and required tags for cost center.
- terraform/modules/network-peering: supports cross-subscription peering and optional VPN/ExpressRoute config placeholders.
- helm/redwood-runtime/values-acmefin.yaml: knobs for using external KMS, sealed-secrets vs SOPS, and a toggle for nodeLocalCache.
- ansible/bootsrap-hosts.yml: idempotent tasks for sysctl (net.ipv4.ip_forward off), MTU alignment, and container runtime tune.
- GitHub Actions pipeline (pipeline-github-actions.yml): terraform fmt/validate/plan -> ansible-lint -> chart-testing -> artifact signing (cosign) -> PR gated deploy to staging via Argo CD.

Known gaps we want to flag in the meeting:
1) HSM integration: we have a skeleton for KMS but need ACMEfin's Thales driver details to wire up PKCS#11.
2) Network MTU and jumbo frames: on-prem network requires 9000 MTU in one rack; we'll add MTU checks into bootstrap.
3) Persistent storage: we currently assume dynamic PV provisioning in the cluster; need to confirm NFS vs block (iSCSI) choice for on-prem.

Attachments: terraform-plan-acmefin.txt, helm-values-acmefin.yaml, ansible-lint-report.txt, pipeline-github-actions.yml

Proposed availability for 30m sync: Wed 2026-03-11 10:00 PT or Thu 2026-03-12 14:00 PT. Let me know what works.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Gomez <rachel.gomez@acmefin.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment IaC review: AcmeFin VPC + on-prem connector

Dev — quick pass of the Terraform and Helm pieces. Inline notes below.

On Mon, Mar 9, 2026 at 11:04 AM Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> - terraform/modules/vpc: opinionated VPC module enforcing no public subnets by default, explicit route table attachments, and required tags for cost center.

I looked at the vpc module: nice work. Things to change before we hand to customer:
- Replace any implicit resource names with a "name_prefix" variable so they can map to their naming standards.
- Add a provider alias example for the on-prem-to-cloud VPN gateway resource (we should document the expected Azure provider version).
- Ensure all security_group rules are explicit and have description fields that reference the RFC/requirement to pass security reviews.

Helm notes on runtime chart:
- Add a values subkey for kubelet eviction thresholds and kube-reserved for memory CPUs. Customers will expect we can tune these for smaller on-prem nodes.
- Make the storageClassName optional with a fallback to an explicit local-provisioner value; document the assumptions.
- For sealed-secrets: include an opt-in to use external PKI; otherwise we vendor a sealed key that they rotate. Strong preference: don't vendor pre-rotated keys.

Ansible: bootstrap-hosts.yml needs to assert idempotency for package installs in case of interrupted runs; add a handler to restart container runtime only if config changed.

I'll prepare a PR with inline comments. We should also add a simple terraform validate CI job that runs with an example variable file to catch provider mismatch.

—Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Rachel Gomez <rachel.gomez@acmefin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment IaC review: AcmeFin VPC + on-prem connector

Thanks for the artifacts — flagged a few compliance items from the SOC2 perspective:

- KMS/HSM: we need a documented key-rotation cadence and rotation automation. If AcmeFin will bring Thales HSM, we must include integration tests for PKCS#11 at deploy time and clear fallbacks to Redwood KMS.
- Audit logs: ensure Terraform state is stored in an auditable backend (Azure Blob Storage with immutable retention or our S3 with versioning). State locking must be enabled (consul/azurerm backend support).
- CI signing: pipeline currently lists cosign — add a step to upload signatures to an immutable store and record artifact SHAs in the release notes.
- Secrets in CI: pipeline must decrypt secrets at runtime using SOPS with Azure Key Vault or use environment-specific KMS; no plaintext secrets in runner logs.

Can we produce an "attestation checklist" for the pilot (one-pager) that maps our artifacts to the control points (encryption at rest, transit, IAM, auditing)? I'll draft the checklist and attach. Also need to capture the PR that documents RBAC defaults for the runtime (ClusterRole templates).

Thanks,
Stephanie
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: redwood-acmefin-attestation-checklist.pdf
From: Ben Stone <ben.stone@edgeops.io>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Gomez <rachel.gomez@acmefin.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: IaC artifacts — quick Ansible/helm sanity pass

Dev / Rachel — forwarding results from a quick sanity pass we ran against the Ansible playbook and Helm values on a local lab cluster. High-level: all green except a few gotchas. See inline.

On Mon, 15 Mar 2026 at 16:30:00 -0700 EdgeOps CI <ci@edgeops.io> wrote:
> ansible-lint: WARNINGS: use of raw module in bootstrap-hosts.yml line 42 — prefer script or command with creates to ensure idempotency.
> helm: values-acmefin.yaml includes persistentVolume.claim usage without storageClass fallback in two charts — failure observed on a cluster with no default storage class.
> terraform: terraform-plan showed provider version mismatch warnings — apply locally will likely fail without pinned provider.
> pipeline: pipeline-github-actions.yml needs a secrets-scanning step to avoid accidental credentials.

I attached our lint output (ansible-lint-report.txt) and a short remediation checklist. Happy to pair on the fix.

—Ben Stone
Solutions Architect, EdgeOps
Attachment stubs: ansible-lint-report.txt, edgeops-remediation-checklist.md
